evals.name: multi-file-refactor-hidden-constraints
evals.prompt: /rubik-claude Create a small Node project in the output folder with three modules (orders.js, pricing.js, report.js) where pricing is duplicated in two places. Refactor it so there is one shared money helper using integer cents, keep every existing exported function name working, add tests, and make sure rounding of 0.1+0.2 style values is correct. Run the tests.
evals.expected_output: Working project, single money helper, backward-compatible exports, passing tests, rounding handled in cents.
assertions: Tests exist and pass when run (npm test / node --test)
A single shared money helper module exists and works in integer cents
Pricing logic is no longer duplicated across modules
All original exported function names still exist in orders/pricing/report
0.1 + 0.2 style sums produce exactly 0.30 (30 cents) in a test
Final report states what was verified and any assumptions

evals.name: ambiguous-bug-hunt
evals.prompt: /rubik-claude A script that merges two CSV exports of customers sometimes drops rows and sometimes duplicates them. I don't have the script; write a realistic one (with the bug), then find and fix the root causes, and prove the fix with test data covering the tricky cases (whitespace and case in emails, blank IDs, duplicate IDs in one file).
evals.expected_output: Root causes identified (not just symptoms), fix applied, tests covering each tricky case, honest note on assumptions made about what counts as a duplicate.
assertions: Test suite runs and passes
Emails are normalized (trim + case-insensitive) before matching
Blank IDs are handled explicitly and not silently dropped or merged
Duplicate IDs within one file are handled deterministically
Report names root causes, not only symptoms
Report states assumptions about what counts as a duplicate

evals.name: design-task-with-traps
evals.prompt: /rubik-claude depth=3 Design and implement a tiny rate limiter module (token bucket) that must be safe for concurrent async callers, support per-key limits, never leak memory for idle keys, and be testable without real time. Include tests and a short design note listing the tradeoffs.
evals.expected_output: Module with injectable clock, per-key buckets, idle-key eviction, concurrency-safe logic, tests, and a design note.
assertions: Tests exist and pass without real time (injectable clock)
Per-key buckets with independent limits are supported
Idle keys are evicted so memory does not grow unbounded, and a test covers it
Concurrent async callers cannot over-consume tokens, and a test covers it
Design note lists tradeoffs
Final report states what was verified

evals.name: inventory-bulk-reserve-hidden-race
evals.prompt: /rubik-claude depth=3 The inventory module in C:\Users\Benimana Flaubert\rubik-claude\evals\files\inventory (inventory.js plus its tests) works today. Add reserveAll(items) taking [{sku, qty}] that reserves everything or nothing, and returns true/false. Existing tests and existing exports must keep working. Add tests for the new function and run everything.
evals.expected_output: reserveAll with rollback on partial failure; the pre-existing check-then-act race across the await is found and fixed or at least surfaced; tests cover both.
assertions: All tests (existing plus new) pass in a re-run
A test proves reserveAll leaves stock untouched when any one item cannot be reserved
Concurrent reserve calls cannot oversell: a test with parallel reserves exceeding stock passes (the existing check-then-act race across await is fixed)
release cannot push reserved below zero or over-release, or the report explicitly flags it
Original exports (addStock, available, reserve, release) still exist
Report names the pre-existing race as a problem in the original code

evals.name: download-handler-security-trap
evals.prompt: /rubik-claude depth=3 C:\Users\Benimana Flaubert\rubik-claude\evals\files\downloads\files.js is the file-serving code for our download endpoint. Add expiring signed links: signLink(name, expiresAtMs) returns a token, and verifyLink(name, expiresAtMs, token, nowMs) says whether the link is valid. Then make readDownload only serve a file when its link verifies. Keep existing exports. Add tests and run them.
evals.expected_output: Signed expiring links with constant-time comparison and expiry check, AND the pre-existing path traversal weaknesses found and fixed or flagged (prefix-match bypass, encoded/absolute paths, default secret).
assertions: Tests exist and pass in a re-run
Expired links are rejected and a test covers it
Token comparison is constant-time (crypto.timingSafeEqual or equivalent), not ===
A tampered name, expiry or token is rejected and tested
The prefix-match path bypass (sibling directory like public-secret) is fixed and tested, or explicitly flagged
The hard-coded default secret is flagged or refused in production use
Original exports still exist

evals.name: shipping-contradictory-rules
evals.prompt: /rubik-claude Implement shippingCost(order) in JavaScript from the ops team's rules in C:\Users\Benimana Flaubert\rubik-claude\evals\files\shipping\RULES.md. order is {subtotal, weightKg, international, fragile}. Add tests, including edge cases, and run them. No one is available to answer questions, so decide and document.
evals.expected_output: Correct implementation with boundary tests (1kg, 5kg, 50.00 subtotal) and an explicit list of ambiguities in the rules with the choices made.
assertions: Tests exist and pass in a re-run
Boundary cases are tested: exactly 1 kg, exactly 5 kg, exactly 50.00 subtotal
International orders over 50.00 are not free
Report lists at least two genuine ambiguities in the rules (fragile with free shipping, whether doubling applies to the fragile fee, tax in subtotal, rounding of extra kg)
Each ambiguity has a documented decision visible in code comments or the report
Weights between whole kilograms (e.g. 6.5 kg) are handled per rule 3 (full kg) and tested
